name: Done-for-you AI support agents for SMBs
one_liner: Set up AI customer-support or chat agents for small businesses and charge a monthly fee to keep them running.
customer: Local and small businesses with heavy customer enquiries
offer: An AI support agent trained on the business's own information, plus monitoring and automated monthly reports
how_it_makes_money: A $2-3K setup fee plus a $500-1,000/month retainer. Build cost was about $50
time_to_first_revenue: unknown (weeks, if you sell a template that is already built)
tools: Docspot or similar AI agent platform; automated reporting
risks: Many competitors and fast commoditisation; Hallucination and GDPR liability in the UK and EU; Churn if results aren't visible; The guest sells the platform, so his claims are biased

name: Remote-managed residential cleaning business
one_liner: Run a recurring house-cleaning company from a distance: the owner handles sales, scheduling and customer service, and contractor cleaners do the work on site.
customer: Homeowners and households in an affluent local market that pay for recurring cleans
offer: Recurring residential cleaning (weekly, biweekly or monthly) plus one-off deep cleans
how_it_makes_money: Per-clean fees, most of them recurring. Margin is the gap between the client price and the contractor cleaner's pay. Recurring clients raise the revenue floor each month.
startup_cost: low (amount not stated; the coaching program was described as 'not cheap')
time_to_first_revenue: unknown (started March 2024; reached $130K/mo after about 2 years 3 months)
tools: booking/CRM software; paid local ads; VA for customer service
risks: Finding and keeping reliable cleaners; Quality control from a distance; The videos are promotional content for a paid coaching academy; UK employment status rules and insurance for contractor cleaners

name: Conversion-focused sites for local trades, prospected with AI

offer: A mobile-first, one-page website with one call to action, reviews placed near the top and tap-to-call, plus ongoing conversion work

startup_cost: low (AI agent and site builder subscriptions; no amount stated)

name: White-label GoHighLevel SaaS for one local niche
one_liner: Rebrand GoHighLevel as a CRM, booking and AI phone system for a single niche and sell it as a subscription.
customer: Local service businesses in one niche, such as med spas, dentists, pest control, roofers or bounce-house rental
offer: A niche-branded all-in-one CRM with marketing, booking, phone and AI features
how_it_makes_money: Monthly SaaS fees, with $97/month as the platform minimum and most resellers charging $200-500. The platform costs $497/month flat, so margins are high
time_to_first_revenue: unknown
risks: Revenue figures are estimates from public award tiers, not verified; Hard to differentiate; Support load and churn; Dependence on GoHighLevel's platform

name: Brand-and-subcontract home service company
one_liner: Run the brand, website, CRM and sales for a home service and pass every job to licensed subcontractors.
customer: Homeowners who need plumbing installs or cleaning
offer: Booked and managed home-service jobs, done by partner tradespeople
how_it_makes_money: Margin between the job price and what the subcontractor is paid
startup_cost: low (about $500 setup; about $300/month for tools plus about $180/month insurance)
time_to_first_revenue: days to weeks; the case reached $81K revenue in its third month (85 days in)
risks: Exact service and margins are not in the excerpt; UK Gas Safe and other licensing and liability rules; Quality control of subcontractors; Phone-heavy sales

name: Semi-trailer leasing arbitrage
one_liner: Lease trailers from a large supplier and sublease them at a markup to truckers who have poor credit.
customer: Owner-operator truck drivers who can't get trailer financing
offer: Monthly rental of 53ft dry van and flatbed trailers
how_it_makes_money: Spread between lease cost (about $350/month) and rental price (about $750/month) per trailer
startup_cost: low (insurance only, according to the founder)
time_to_first_revenue: Immediate with the first renter. He was at $7,500/month recurring within 2 months
risks: US market only. The UK HGV trailer market and its credit dynamics are untested; Renters default on payment, and trailers get damaged or stolen; Depends on a supplier willing to lease trailers to you

name: Mail-in home video, photo and slide digitisation
one_liner: Customers post their old VHS/camcorder tapes, photos and slides to you; you send back digital files and the originals.
customer: Families, often after a bereavement, who have tapes they can't play any more
offer: Tape-to-digital transfer delivered as a download or flash drive, with photo and slide scanning as add-ons
how_it_makes_money: Per tape ($15–$30) or per hour of footage (A RS Video charges $18.75–$25/hr with a $25 minimum). The video's example: 15 tapes a week at $25 is about $1,600 a month
startup_cost: low (~$200 capture device plus a used VCR and a computer you already have; 'a few hundred' all in)
time_to_first_revenue: about 3 months in the case example (first paid job in month 3)
tools: USB capture device; used VCR; computer; Google Business Profile; Facebook groups; tracked postage (Royal Mail / CTT)
risks: Large national competitors (Legacybox, iMemories) keep prices around $15 per tape; Labour is real-time, so 1 hour of tape takes about 1 hour of capture; Liability if irreplaceable originals are lost or damaged in the post; Demand shrinks as the supply of old tapes runs out

name: Email list and newsletter monetisation for small businesses
one_liner: Done-for-you service that uses AI connected to newsletter tools (Beehiiv MCP) to turn a small business's dormant email list into campaigns, automations and a community.
customer: Local and niche small businesses that already have an email list (plumbers, real estate, etc.)
offer: Setting up and running email campaigns, automations and a paid or free community
how_it_makes_money: Monthly retainer; the example given is $1,000/month to generate $12,000/month for the client
startup_cost: low (AI subscription plus the client's own Beehiiv account)
time_to_first_revenue: unknown; plausibly weeks
risks: Weak evidence: the revenue figures are hypothetical and the video is sponsor-style; Proving ROI to the client; Sales to small-business owners usually needs calls

name: Niche vibe-coded micro-SaaS (digital waivers for youth or church groups)
one_liner: An AI-built simple app that solves one painful workflow for a narrow group, such as e-signed liability waivers for youth activities.
customer: Church youth leaders, clubs, activity organisers
offer: A simple niche web app for collecting signed waivers by mobile link, replacing PDF printing
how_it_makes_money: Subscription or per-event fee (pricing not stated)
time_to_first_revenue: The goal was a sale within the 85-minute video; the result isn't shown in the excerpt
tools: Replit Agent; Claude; Namecheap; Facebook ads; Reddit
risks: Existing tools (DocuSign, Smartwaiver) compete; Hard to find customers without an audience; GDPR and child data handling; Maintenance and the 'last mile' of finishing the product

name: Personalised 3D-printed products on Etsy
one_liner: Start with a few home printers and sell custom or niche 3D-printed products on Etsy, then grow into your own store.
customer: Etsy shoppers buying personalised gifts and niche items
offer: Custom and own-design 3D-printed products (started with 3D-scanned head figurines)
how_it_makes_money: Product margin of about 50% on own designs. Revenue went from $50K in year 1 to $400K in year 2 and nearly $1M in total
startup_cost: low to start (a couple of printers), growing to about $100K of machines
time_to_first_revenue: unknown (sold on Etsy soon after starting about 2.5 years ago; year 1 = $50K)

name: AI-built websites for local businesses

name: Niche low-competition e-commerce brand (e.g. stainless steel litter box)
one_liner: Build a brand around one high-search, low-keyword-difficulty product that has a single dominant seller.
customer: Online consumers searching for a specific product (e.g. cat owners)

how_it_makes_money: Product margin; the incumbent sells at $358
time_to_first_revenue: unknown; the creator says one product did $15K in its first month

name: Leased event venue rented by the hour or day
one_liner: Lease a cheap retail or church unit with good parking, fit it out on a budget, and rent it for parties, showers and Sunday church services, with online booking.
customer: Families hosting birthdays, baby showers and anniversaries, plus small churches needing a weekly space
offer: Venue hire with modern online booking and availability (the competitors studied used paper calendars)
how_it_makes_money: Hourly or daily hire fees. Three churches paying every Sunday cover the whole rent, and party bookings are profit. A QR code on the wall drives referrals
startup_cost: low-medium (could do it 'for under 3,000', plus the lease)
time_to_first_revenue: Fast once the space is found: $100 of Facebook ads brought $10,000 of bookings in one day
tools: Online booking calendar; Facebook ads; QR referral code
risks: Lease commitment and planning/use-class rules in the UK; Parking makes or breaks the site; Property damage and noise complaints (e.g. 'a goat hanging from the ceiling'); Needs someone local for check-ins and cleaning

name: AI-assisted freelance retainers via Upwork (SEO/AI services)
one_liner: Apply to Upwork jobs in AI and SEO and deliver the work with ChatGPT, then turn single clients into monthly retainers.
